title: Unraveling the multifaceted relationship between creativity and mental health with longitudinal analyses of genotyped twins
title_zh: 揭示创意与心理健康之间多面关系：基于基因分型双胞胎的纵向分析
abstract: Abstract Existing findings of creativity and mental health associations are inconsistent, partly due to heterogeneous assessment of creativity and mental health. Consequently, basic questions concerning the direction and domain specificity of these associations remain unanswered. This comprehensive study used data from 14 658 Swedish twins, including a genotyped subsample, and employed a range of genetically informed and longitudinal designs to examine the direction, nature, and underlying mechanisms of the creativity–mental health relationship. Creativity was assessed broadly, using different measures of artistic and scientific achievement, occupation, personality (openness), and psychometric creativity (divergent thinking). Mental health was measured using both self-report data and registry-based diagnoses. Higher artistic creativity, as indexed by artistic achievement and openness, was associated with worse mental health (e.g., psychosis proneness, major depressive disorder, and anxiety disorder). In contrast, measures of scientific creativity showed predominantly non-significant, or even negative, associations with mental health problems, particularly in the case of occupational creativity. Co-twin control and polygenic score analyses suggested that shared genetic factors played an important role in the observed associations, with the exception of a potential causal association between depressive symptoms and openness, which persisted even in the longitudinal co-twin control model. Genetic correlations further showed shared underlying genetic influences. In summary, our findings offer novel evidence for a complex, bidirectional, and genetically influenced association between artistic creativity and mental health, helping to clarify mixed results in the prior literature.
abstract_zh: 摘要 现有关于创意与心理健康关联的研究结果不一致，部分原因在于对创意和心理健康的评估方式异质性。因此，关于这些关联的方向和领域特异性等基本问题仍未得到解答。本综合研究利用了14,658名瑞典双胞胎的数据，其中包括一个基因分型子样本，并采用多种基因信息和纵向设计来检验创意-心理健康关系的方向、性质及其潜在机制。创意的评估范围广泛，涵盖艺术和科学成就、职业、人格（开放性）以及心理测量创意（发散性思维）。心理健康则通过自我报告数据和基于登记的诊断来测量。以艺术成就和开放性为指标的高艺术创意与较差的心理健康相关（如精神病倾向、重度抑郁障碍和焦虑障碍）。相反，科学创意的测量主要与心理健康问题呈非显著或负相关，尤其是在职业创意的情况下。双胞胎控制和多基因评分分析表明，共享的遗传因素在观察到的关联中起重要作用，唯一例外是抑郁症状与开放性之间可能存在的因果关联，即使在纵向双胞胎控制模型中也持续存在。遗传相关性进一步显示共享的潜在遗传影响。总之，我们的发现为艺术创意与心理健康之间的复杂、双向且受遗传影响的关联提供了新证据，有助于阐明先前文献中的混杂结果。
